# `Scanner/T1Vial-v0` · Measure T1 of each marked vial

**A · Signal and contrast** · spins and relaxation · kind 1, measure · isolates A4: T1: recovery of the longitudinal magnetisation. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** CANDIDATE: the gate has not been run (no stored result)

T1 by inversion recovery, the reference method of relaxometry, as one skill. At a fixed repetition time the signal of a vial is a - b exp(-TI / T1) with the true T1, whatever the repetition time, the inversion efficiency and the slice profile are, so three signed inversion times give T1. What has to be decided is the timing: the budget sets the repetition time, and the inversion times have to span the recovery of every vial. The transmitter is calibrated; Scanner/T1Transmit is the task with a transmit error. Measurement task or decision task (does a fixed list of scans pass within 25 points of the reference?): not determined, the gate result is not stored yet.

Kind of task: **undetermined** (no stored gate result).

- Sequences that matter here: ir

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'t1_ms': {'<region id>': '<milliseconds>'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; deliverable valid: exactly the region ids, values in 10 to 20000 ms
- Error: `largest over the regions of |ln(T1_delivered / T1_true)|`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates and, for every region, error <= ln(1.1)

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

**Gate not stored on this engine** (`mrgym-engine-0.2.0`). `mrgym gate Scanner/T1Vial-v0 --n 300 --write` measures and stores it.

| Policy | Must | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reference` | pass | inversion recovery, three or four inversion times spread over the recovery, signed three-parameter fit |
| `prior` | fail | no scan; the geometric mean of the told T1 range in every region |
| `fixed_recipe` | fail | one token scan, then one constant T1 for every region, tuned on other worlds |
| `brute_force` | fail | inversion times on a grid; T1 = (inversion time of the smallest magnitude) / ln 2 |
| `wrong_units` | fail | the reference's numbers in seconds |
| `unsigned` | ablation | the reference's scans fitted to magnitudes, without the sign |
| `full_recovery` | ablation | the reference's scans fitted with M (1 - 2 exp(-TI / T1)) (assumes full recovery and a complete inversion) |
| `bunched_tis` | ablation | three inversion times around the expected nulls instead of spread over the recovery |
| `level1_scans` | ablation | the three scans level 1 states, at every level |
| `open_loop` | reported | the level's fixed scan list and the least-squares fit of the three-parameter curve |

## What the agent reads at reset (level 1, seed 0)

~~~text
# Measure T1 of each marked vial
A test object with vials of unknown materials lies in the field of view.
Deliver the longitudinal relaxation time T1 of each marked region, in milliseconds, with `submit`.
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre; each lies inside one homogeneous material):
  R1: y -15.72, x -54.18, radius 11.5
  R2: y 53.81, x -20.03, radius 11.5
  R3: y -48.9, x 18.97, radius 11.5
T1 values lie between 300 and 1500 ms. Nothing else about the object is known, and the noise level is not given.
The transmit calibration is correct: at the slice centre the flip angle is the nominal one, everywhere in the object.
Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; they are charged to the scan-time budget.
A region read-out is a mean over the image as reconstructed: with partial Fourier the zero-filled lines mix the
material around a vial into it.

Passing: for every region the delivered T1 lies within a factor 1.1 of the true T1 (between T1 / 1.1 and 1.1 x T1).
The scanner's log must show that you measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong.

How to do it (this level states the procedure).
  1. Run three inversion-recovery scans: sequence ir, tr_ms 1500, matrix 32 (no partial Fourier), with
     ti_ms 30, 400 and 1450. Each costs 52.5 s. Read out the marked regions.
  2. Sign the read-outs. At ti_ms 1450 every material is past its null, so its signal is positive: S3 =
     `complex_mean_magnitude`. A read-out of the same region whose `complex_mean_phase_rad` differs from that of the
     ti_ms 1450 scan by more than pi / 2 (after wrapping the difference into -pi .. pi) is negative: S = -magnitude.
  3. At a fixed repetition time the signal is exactly S(TI) = a - b exp(-TI / T1). a and b drop out of
         q = (S3 - S2) / (S2 - S1) = (exp(-400 / T1) - exp(-1450 / T1)) / (exp(-30 / T1) - exp(-400 / T1)).
     The right side grows with T1. Find the T1 at which it equals the measured q, by bisection between 50 and 5000 ms.
  4. Deliver that T1 in milliseconds for the region.
Do not use S = M (1 - 2 exp(-TI / T1)): it assumes a repetition time of many T1 and a complete inversion.

Limits. Scan time: 165 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 40 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
[scan time left 165.00 of 165 s · calls 0/40 · rejected 0/8]
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier reads the hidden T1 and scans nothing.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
